s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive abdominal distension with early satiety and urinary urgency
salient_findings: Large midline intraperitoneal cyst compressing adjacent abdominal organs
Cyst measuring 16 × 24 cm on ultrasonography and 30 × 25.6 × 16.8 cm on computed tomography
key_facts: 23-year-old woman
2-year history of progressive abdominal distension
Early satiety
Urinary urgency
No pain, weight loss, or systemic symptoms
Normal menstrual cycles
Mother had a history of ovarian cysts
Abdomen distended with dull percussion notes but without tenderness or guarding
Large midline intraperitoneal cyst on imaging
Cyst had a fluid density of 20 Hounsfield units
No calcifications, soft-tissue components, or enhancing septations on imaging
Laboratory studies, including tumor markers, were within normal limits
ROMA score was 4.1 %
Serological testing for Echinococcus granulosus was negative

shortlist.label: Mesenteric cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Large midline intraperitoneal cyst on imaging

shortlist.label: Omental cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Cyst had a fluid density of 20 Hounsfield units and demonstrated no calcifications, soft-tissue components, or enhancing septations

shortlist.label: Simple ovarian cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Mother had a history of ovarian cysts and patient has a large cyst involving the uterus and ovaries

shortlist.label: Mucinous cystadenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive abdominal distension and large cyst size

shortlist.label: Serous cystadenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Benign etiology suggested by imaging and laboratory studies

raw.rationale: The large midline intraperitoneal cyst with a fluid density of 20 Hounsfield units and no calcifications, soft-tissue components, or enhancing septations on imaging, along with the patient's symptoms of abdominal distension, early satiety, and urinary urgency, are consistent with a mesenteric cyst. The location and size of the cyst, as well as the absence of tumor markers and a low ROMA score, support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Simple ovarian cyst
rejected.why: The cyst's large size and midline location are not typical of a simple ovarian cyst, which is usually smaller and located on the ovary.

rejected.label: Mucinous cystadenoma
rejected.why: The absence of tumor markers and a low ROMA score, as well as the lack of soft-tissue components or enhancing septations on imaging, make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Serous cystadenoma
rejected.why: Similar to mucinous cystadenoma, the lack of tumor markers and a low ROMA score, along with the imaging characteristics, make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Omental cyst
rejected.why: While possible, the location and size of the cyst, as well as the patient's symptoms, are more consistent with a mesenteric cyst.
